STAGE 1 - scoring pass over the rubric (rubric-2026-10-v1) for A=cocond-markov-poincare-ot vs B=CURVCELL-SID.
READ: full prompt (both idea specs + shared evidence bundle ids E1-E13).
OBSERVED: (i) geometry - A's curved ops are the Poincare Sinkhorn ground cost (bc19762831440f87 E12/E13) plus a Klein/Einstein hyperbolic barycenter codebook update, which has no Euclidean counterpart; B's only behavioural degree of freedom is a scalar s[l][k]=sqrt(kappa) dividing the Poincare distance (e9e97242e0e9ed08 E12/E13), so a matched Euclidean per-code scale ||eps-c||/s reproduces the same cell-boundary shift -> rubric level 2 for B. (ii) behaviour - B's branching statistic is directly measured: e9e97242e0e9ed08 E5 gives H=0.931/support 2.8/top1 0.438 up to H=3.405/support 44.3/top1 0.054, bin1 n=4895, and E10 gives 115582 distinct edges, mean out-degree 5.45; A's relevant statistic is weak, E11 same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067 (1.35x), and E8 shows the level-1 ceiling at K=256 is only 0.0822 (0.3106 at K=16). (iii) falsifiability - A specifies diffusion-off (alpha=0), curvature-off and a baseline, plus a discriminating diagnostic and explicit refutation; B's geometry-off keeps "behaviour weights but removes curvature", but the weights only act through the curvature, so behaviour-off and geometry-off collapse to the same fixed-curvature baseline (single, non-discriminating control).
REASONING: weighting the rubric, A leads on geometry_necessity (20), novelty (20), downstream (15), falsifiability (10), exploration (5); B leads on behaviour_evidence (20) and implementability (10). Rough scores A 3.6, B 3.25. A also has the harder failure mode (in-batch transition matrix near identity), which goes into FAILURE RISK.
OPEN: confirm the in-batch sparsity arithmetic before writing the final record.

STAGE 2 - check of A's diffusion channel before finalising.
READ: A specification step (4) 'P <- (1-alpha)*P + alpha*(B_bt @ P)' and step (5) argmax, versus evidence bundle stats.
OBSERVED: B_bt is a BxB operator over the batch (B=1024) while the measured graph has mean out-degree 5.4526 (bc19762831440f87 E10). With a catalogue on the order of 2.5e4 items, the expected number of a row's successors co-present in a 1023-item batch is ~5.45*1023/24556 ~ 0.23, so B_bt ~ 0.23*A + 0.77*I and one diffusion step adds only ~alpha*0.23 of neighbour mass. A itself lists this degenerate case in RISKS ('B_bt close to the identity, degrading the mechanism to plain curved Sinkhorn'). This lowers A's behaviour_evidence to ~2-3 and implementability to ~2, but does not flip the weighted comparison (A still ~3.4-3.6 vs B ~3.25).
REASONING: keep A as winner, make the in-batch identity case the named failure risk, since it is the single thing most likely to make the choice wrong.
OPEN: none; final answer to be appended.

STAGE 3 - FINAL ANSWER (complete, stands alone).
WINNER: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
FIRST LISTED: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
ARGUMENT: (1) geometry_necessity+novelty: A's given curvature is not a rescaled distance - the entropic-OT ground cost is the Poincare metric and the codebook step is a closed-form Klein/Einstein hyperbolic barycenter, which has no Euclidean equivalent and is argued against the matched Euclidean control (Euclidean cost kernel + Euclidean weighted mean); B's behaviour signal enters only as one scalar s[l][k] dividing the Poincare distance (bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08 E12/E13), so a matched Euclidean per-code scale reproduces the same cell-boundary shift (rubric level 2), and per-branch curvature is already on this ledger, making B a routine variation while A moves the assignment plan, which no listed round did. (2) downstream+falsifiability: A names the change (level-l code choice and barycenter weights), two observables with expected direction (first-two-token prefix hit-rate, conditional code-usage entropy) and the Stage-3 threshold 0.065 against the measured band l1_only 0.06233 / l1_br_euclid 0.06207 / resample 0.06363 on 57,439 rows (E6), plus an explicit refutation (prefix hit rises while recall does not -> decorative structure); B's geometry-off control is degenerate because the behaviour weights act only through curvature, so behaviour-off and geometry-off both collapse to fixed-curvature baseline and the control does not isolate the switch. (3) behaviour_evidence favours B - E5 gives measured branching heterogeneity H 0.931/support 2.8/top1 0.438 to H 3.405/support 44.3/top1 0.054 over 4895 items in bin 1 and E10 gives 115,582 edges at mean out-degree 5.45, while A's relevant statistic is thin (E11 same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067; E8 level-1 sharing ceiling 0.0822 at K=256) - but that is 20% of the rubric against the 70% where A is stronger, so A still scores higher overall (~3.4-3.6 vs ~3.25).
FAILURE RISK: A's diffusion may be inert: B_bt is a 1024x1024 batch-restricted operator, and with mean out-degree 5.4526 (E10) over a catalogue of ~2.5e4 a row has only ~0.23 successors inside the same 1023-item batch, so B_bt is near identity, the plan reduces to plain curved Sinkhorn, and the run would be read as a curvature null when the behaviour channel was never exercised; separately, if K=256 level-1 sharing cannot exceed the measured 0.0822 ceiling (E8), even a working plan cannot raise first-two-token prefix hits enough to clear 0.065.

CHECK: head-to-head of cocond-markov-poincare-ot (A) vs CURVCELL-SID (B) on rubric-2026-10-v1, frozen bundles 404ea254563870a6 / bc19762831440f87 / e9e97242e0e9ed08.
READ: both idea specs; evidence E5 (successor-entropy stratification, top1 0.4375->0.0543, Spearman -0.973), E6 (width-20 beam survival; l1_br 0.04671, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363, successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500), E7 (per-position NLL), E8 (first-level capacity ceiling: K=256 -> 0.0822 shared cluster vs K=16 -> 0.3106), E10 (edge_density 5.33, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526, 118315 edges), E11 (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067). E12/E13 for both are PROPOSED geometric descriptions only.
OBSERVED: A's core (curved Sinkhorn/geodesic successor matching) is the family already measured and already below the Euclidean control in E6 (0.0550/0.0546 vs 0.06207), and A's own acknowledged sparsity risk is quantified by E10 (out-degree 5.45) so the B_bt diffusion is near-identity for most rows, collapsing to the measured-underperforming curved Sinkhorn. A also leaves alpha and the usage prior q as "measured, never tuned" with no measurement rule -> implementability gap. B's per-code sizing targets the bottleneck E8 actually names (capacity ceiling at K=256 is 0.0822), specifies closed-form s update, refresh schedule, cumulative-mean smoothing, clamps, no gradient into s, +2-4% cost, and names the assignment (argmin + commitment), the observable (H(next code|level-0)), the direction (down) and the diagnostic (Spearman |A_k| vs B_k). B's weakness: dividing Poincare distance by s[k] is a per-code radial rescale that a weighted Euclidean distance could mimic, so geometry_necessity is only ~3, and the EM loop can collapse/oscillate.
OPEN: neither reaches the 0.065 recall bar in E6 (max measured 0.06363), so both hypotheses are above the observed ceiling; this is a shared weakness, not a discriminator.

ANSWER: WINNER: CURVCELL-SID. FIRST LISTED: cocond-markov-poincare-ot. Rationale recorded in the previous stage: E6 shows A's curved-successor family already measured below the Euclidean control (0.0550/0.0546 vs 0.06207), E10 quantifies the sparsity that degrades A's Markov diffusion (out-degree 5.45) while E8 quantifies the cell-capacity bottleneck B addresses (0.0822 at K=256), and B is the only one with a closed-form, budgeted, differentiable specification plus matched behaviour-off and geometry-off controls and a discriminating diagnostic. Failure risk of B: the per-code curvature rescale is a radial scale that a weighted Euclidean distance can reproduce, and the EM fixed point can collapse to a few huge low-curvature cells or oscillate at refresh epochs, leaving recall at baseline.

STAGE 1 - Read both finalists and the frozen bundle; goal: fix the comparison axes before scoring.
READ: IDEA A cocond-markov-poincare-ot (bundle bc19762831440f87) and IDEA B CURVCELL-SID (bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08); both bundles share the same OBSERVED rows E4-E11 (E5 successor-entropy bins, E6 width-20 beam survival on 57,439 test rows, E7 teacher-forced per-position NLL, E8 first-level capacity ceiling, E10 train-only edge density, E11 same-first-prefix rate vs permuted null).
OBSERVED FACTS I will lean on:
- E11: same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted_null 0.067 -> the SID successor structure is real but only barely above chance; headroom is small for both.
- E6: every behaviour-conditioned SID measured so far is BELOW its Euclidean control: successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500 vs l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363. l1_br (branching) is the WORST at 0.04671.
- E7: l1_br has T1/T2/T3 NLL 0.00/0.00/0.00 and T4 9.03 -> the level-1 conditional entropy of that branching variant is already pinned to ~0 while recall is the worst measured.
- E8: cluster-share of canonical pairs falls from 0.3106 (K=16) to 0.0822 (K=256) -> prefix capacity is a K-level lever, which neither finalist changes (both keep K=256 per level).
OPEN: which of the two is a distinct computation vs a re-run of a measured negative; whether A's batch-coupled plan and B's encoder-cancellable rescaling are fatal.

STAGE 2 - Scored both on rubric-2026-10-v1; goal: decide which to run first.
reasoning (dimension: score A / score B):
- behavior_evidence (20%): 3-4 / 3-4. Both name the same measured problem (E11 0.0907 vs 0.067; E6 gold-prefix-alive at depth 4 = 0.068-0.088 over 57,439 rows). A's own remedy direction is pressured by E6 (successor family below euclid); B's by E6/E7 (l1_br worst at 0.04671). No edge.
- geometry_necessity (20%): 2 / 2. A uses fixed kappa=-1: the behavioural content sits in the Markov diffusion, the curved cost/Einstein midpoint is Euclidean-reproducible near the origin and no matched control is specified. B's per-code d_B/s is exactly reproducible by Euclidean ||eps-c||/s, and B itself concedes the rescaled distance is not a metric. A slightly the stronger only because curvature enters the cost kernel nonlinearly, not just as a scale.
- novelty (20%): 4 / 2. A moves the assignment PLAN itself (entropic-OT plan diffused one Markov step along training transitions + closed-form Klein/Einstein barycenter codebook), which is not in the ledger (geodesic rank, fork-angle transport, shells, Lorentz cones, tangent residual, per-branch curvature). B is a per-code rewrite of the already-measured branch-count curvature family: same statistic (E5 branching), same insertion point (level-1 argmin + commitment).
- downstream_mechanism (15%): 3 / 4. A's chain is specific but its observable (prefix hit-rate) is entangled with batch-dependent SIDs. B's chain names the assignment, the observable and the direction cleanly; its weakness is that the diagnostic is already saturated (E7 T1-T3 NLL 0.00 for l1_br).
- falsifiability (10%): 4 / 3. A states both switches (behaviour-off changes plan+barycenter weights, curvature-off changes cost kernel+mean operator) and a discriminating fallback (prefix hit-rate up but recall flat => decorative). B's refuter (|A_k| vs B_k ~ 0 => redundant) is non-discriminating because l1_br already achieves near-zero conditional entropy with the worst recall.
- implementability (10%): 2 / 4. A leaves alpha and q "measured, never tuned (see SAFEGUARDS)" with no SAFEGUARDS text supplied, and its plan update P <- (1-alpha)P + alpha*(B_bt @ P) makes each item's SID depend on minibatch composition, with no inference-time rule. B is per-item deterministic, +2-4% step time, L*K scalars, no new parameters, tanh/clamp guarded, no gradient into s.
- exploration_value (5%): 3 / 1. A is a different failure mode (plan-level reallocation). B is a near-repeat of the measured branching negative in E6/E7.
Weighted verdict: A wins novelty (+2 on 20%) and exploration (+1 on 5%); B wins implementability (+2 on 10%). Net favours A; the deciding qualitative point is that B's headline diagnostic is already saturated in the ledger (E7) while A's has not been measured.
Overturns nothing from stage 1.

STAGE 3 - Final answer (complete, stands alone).
WINNER: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
FIRST LISTED: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
ARGUMENT: (1) novelty (20%) and exploration_value (5%): cocond changes the assignment computation itself - an entropic-OT plan diffused one Markov step along training-only transitions, with a closed-form Klein/Einstein barycenter codebook - a computation absent from the ledger (geodesic rank, fork-angle transport, radial shells, Lorentz cones, tangent residual, per-branch curvature). CURVCELL is a per-code rewrite of the already-measured branch-count curvature family, and that family is the worst measured row in the bundle: E6 l1_br recall@10 0.04671 vs its own Euclidean control l1_br_euclid 0.06207 and resample 0.06363. (2) falsifiability (10%) and downstream_mechanism (15%): CURVCELL's own success criterion - level-1 conditional entropy H(next code | level-0 code) falls, Spearman(|A_k|, B_k) > 0 - is already saturated in the ledger: E7 shows l1_br at T1/T2/T3 NLL 0.00/0.00/0.00 yet E6 recall 0.04671, so the mechanism can declare success on its stated observable with zero recommendation gain; its diagnostic cannot discriminate. cocond instead commits to a prefix-hit-rate observable plus a stated branch (E6-style depth-1/2 survival up but recall flat means the coupling is decorative), which is unmeasured and therefore informative. (3) geometry_necessity (20%) and behavior_evidence (20%): both name the same real, measured problem - E11 same_first_prefix 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067, E6 gold-prefix-alive at depth 4 only 0.068-0.088 over 57,439 test rows - but CURVCELL's curvature only acts through argmin boundaries, so the encoder can cancel it by moving latents (its own named risk) and its rescaled distance is Euclidean-reproducible as ||eps-c||/s; cocond acts on the plan, so the assignment changes without requiring the encoder to cooperate. Evidence ids used: E5, E6, E7, E8, E11.
FAILURE RISK: cocond's plan update P <- (1-alpha)P + alpha*(B_bt @ P) couples items inside one minibatch, so an item's SID depends on batch composition and no inference-time assignment rule is given; alpha and q are deferred to a "SAFEGUARDS" block that is not in the supplied specification, and tau is frozen at the first batch's median distance. If those cannot be pinned to a deterministic per-item rule, cocond is not implementable as written (implementability 2 vs 4) and drops below CURVCELL on the 10% + 15% implementability/downstream weights; additionally E6 already shows successor-informed SIDs underperforming Euclidean (0.05122/0.05500 vs 0.06207), so the whole successor-injection family may be a measured negative and CURVCELL's cheap, deterministic cell rescaling would then have been the better first run.
